name: Semicircular Canal Dehiscence Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Minor and Major Diagnostic Criteria for SSCD

criteria.description: Radiologic evidence of bony dehiscence of the superior semicircular canal on high-resolution CT scan
Abnormal vestibular-evoked myogenic potentials (VEMP) with lowered threshold or increased amplitude
Presence of characteristic symptoms such as sound- or pressure-induced vertigo and autophony
Low-frequency conductive hearing loss on audiometric testing
Exclusion of other vestibular or otologic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiologic evidence of canal dehiscence plus characteristic clinical symptoms and abnormal VEMP testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, audiologic, vestibular, and imaging findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autophony (hearing one's own voice or internal sounds loudly)

searchTerms: sensation of environment moving with head motion

rare.notes: Due to aberrant transmission of sound or pressure
searchTerms: facial muscle twitching from nerve stimulation

rare.symptomName: Hearing loss progression to mixed or sensorineural
searchTerms: hearing loss worsening to nerve-related type

rare.symptomName: Vertigo triggered by straining or Valsalva maneuver
searchTerms: dizziness triggered by straining or breath holding

laboratory: Vestibular-evoked myogenic potentials (VEMP) with lowered threshold and increased amplitude
imaging: High-resolution computed tomography (CT) scan showing bony dehiscence of the superior semicircular canal
other: Audiometry demonstrating low-frequency conductive hearing loss
Clinical examination revealing Tullio phenomenon and Hennebert sign

distinguishingFeatures: Episodic vertigo with fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss
Absence of bony dehiscence on CT imaging
No radiologic evidence of semicircular canal dehiscence

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe vertigo with hearing loss
Neurological deficits such as diplopia or weakness
Signs of intracranial pathology on imaging
references: Minor LB, Solomon D, Zinreich JS, Zee DS. Sound- and pressure-induced vertigo due to bone dehiscence of the superior semicircular canal. N Engl J Med. 1998;339(12): 746-753.
Ward BK, Carey JP, Minor LB. Superior semicircular canal dehiscence syndrome: lessons from the first 20 years. Front Neurol. 2017;8:177.
Rosowski JJ. Superior semicircular canal dehiscence syndrome. Curr Opin Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2009;17(5):356-361.
